skills.rule: If a customer exhibits 3 or more churn signals (e.g., no logins, support ticket escalations, downgrade inquiries) within a 30-day timeframe, an AM call must be scheduled within 24 hours.
skills.rationale: To identify and intervene when accounts show signs of churning.
evidence: If a customer exhibits 3 or more churn signals (e.g., no logins, support ticket escalations, downgrade inquiries) within a 30-day timeframe, you must schedule an AM call within 24 hours.

skills.rule: All new Enterprise customers must have a dedicated kickoff call, a customized training session, and a 30-day check-in.
skills.rationale: Standardized onboarding process for Enterprise tier.
evidence: For all new Enterprise customers, the onboarding process must include a dedicated kickoff call, a customized training session, and a 30-day check-in.

skills.rule: If a P0 (Critical) bug is reported by an Enterprise customer, the on-call engineer must be paged immediately.
skills.rationale: P0 bugs involve system down, data loss, or core workflow breakage; high priority for Enterprise.
evidence: If a P0 bug is reported by an Enterprise customer, page the on-call engineer immediately.

skills.rule: P1 (High) bugs must be resolved within 4 hours.
skills.rationale: P1 bugs represent major features that are broken but have a workaround.
evidence: P1 bugs must be resolved within 4 hours.

skills.rule: If a standard customer SLA is breached by > 1 hour, notify the support lead. If an Enterprise customer SLA is breached by >= 2 hours, notify the Account Manager and Engineering Lead immediately.
skills.rationale: Standard process for monitoring SLA compliance with higher priority for Enterprise tier.
evidence: If a customer SLA is breached by more than 1 hour, notify the support lead.
If an Enterprise plan customer SLA is breached by 2 hours or more, you must notify both the Account Manager and the Engineering Lead immediately.

skills.rule: During an active platform outage, support must not troubleshoot; instead, send the standard incident response template and link to the status page.
skills.rationale: To streamline communication and avoid redundant troubleshooting during outages.
evidence: If a customer contacts support during an active platform outage, do not troubleshoot. Send the standard incident response template and link to the status page.

skills.rule: Founder approval is required for any engineering candidate at the offer stage before the final offer letter is sent.
skills.rationale: Final quality control for engineering hires.
evidence: For any engineering candidate at the offer stage, you must get Founder approval before sending the final offer letter.

skills.rule: A Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is triggered if an employee misses core KPIs for two consecutive quarters; HR must then schedule a formal review with the department head within 5 business days.
evidence: A Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is triggered if an employee misses their core KPIs for two consecutive quarters.
If an employee is placed on a PIP, HR must schedule a formal review with the department head within 5 business days.

skills.rule: Support/CS can approve up to 10% for churn prevention. Early-stage startups (pre-seed/seed) on Annual plans can receive up to 20% for the first year. Discounts > 30% must be escalated to an AE; Support is prohibited from approving these.
skills.rationale: Empowerment of front-line staff while maintaining senior oversight for high-value discounts.
evidence: Support and CS can apply up to a 10% discount to save a churning customer.
If a customer identifies as an early-stage startup (pre-seed or seed), you may approve up to a 20% discount on the Annual plan for the first year.
If a customer requests a discount greater than 30%, it must be escalated to an Account Executive (AE) for approval. Support cannot approve this.

skills.rule: Enterprise customers requesting custom feature bundles or volume-based pricing must be routed to the VP of Sales.
skills.rationale: Centralize complex pricing negotiations at the executive level.
evidence: Enterprise customers requesting custom feature bundles or volume-based pricing must be routed to the VP of Sales.

skills.rule: Annual plans: full refund within 14 days, prorated after 14 days. Enterprise: escalate to AM within 1 hour. LTD: strictly deny. Monthly: escalate to Founder if > $500 and tenure < 3 months. All tiers: deny if purchase > 60 days. Exception: bypass 30-day rule for customers with > 2 years tenure.
skills.rationale: Balance customer satisfaction with revenue protection. Note: Contradiction exists between SOP (60 days) and internal chat (30 days) regarding hard limits; SOP 60-day limit takes precedence.
evidence: If a customer on an annual plan requests a refund within the first 14 days of purchase, approve a full refund immediately.
If a customer on an annual plan requests a refund after 14 days, approve a prorated refund for the remaining unused months.
If any Enterprise customer requests a refund of any amount, DO NOT process it immediately. You must escalate to the Account Manager (AM) within 1 hour.
Under no circumstances do we process refunds for lifetime deal accounts. Deny the request citing LTD terms.
If a customer on a monthly plan with a tenure of less than 3 months requests a refund over $500, escalate to the Founder.
We offer absolutely no refunds after 60 days of purchase for any customer tier. If the purchase was more than 60 days ago, deny the refund.

skills.rule: Any software vendor invoice of $3,500 or more must be routed to the ops lead for approval before payment by finance.
skills.rationale: Financial oversight for high-cost software vendors.
evidence: Any software vendor invoice of $3,500 or more needs to be routed to the ops lead for approval before finance pays it.
